outline: 1013 Angles in a Right Angle and Straight Line

examples.solution_text:
Angles on a straight line add to $180^{\circ}$.

$\begin{aligned}55^{\circ}+60^{\circ}+x&=180^{\circ}\\115^{\circ}+x&=180^{\circ}\\x&=65^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

Angles in a right angle add to $90^{\circ}$.

$\begin{aligned}24^{\circ}+36^{\circ}+x&=90^{\circ}\\60^{\circ}+x&=90^{\circ}\\x&=30^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

Angles at a point add to $360^{\circ}$.

$\begin{aligned}x+65^{\circ}+85^{\circ}&=360^{\circ}\\x+150^{\circ}&=360^{\circ}\\x&=210^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

Angles at a point add to $360^{\circ}$.

$\begin{aligned}b+2b+3b+210&=360\\6b+210&=360\\6b&=150\\b&=25\end{aligned}$

The three unknown angles are $25^{\circ}$, $50^{\circ}$ and $75^{\circ}$.

The whole upper angle is $32^{\circ}+54^{\circ}=86^{\circ}$.

Vertically opposite angles are equal, so $x=86^{\circ}$.

examples.derivation: Straight-line total: x = 180° − 55° − 60° = 65°. Diagram sectors measure 65°, 60° and 55°, matching the labels.
Right-angle total: x = 90° − 24° − 36° = 30°. Rays at 0°, 24°, 60° and 90° produce the stated sectors; the right-angle marker is consistent.
Point total: x = 360° − 65° − 85° = 210°. The arc from 150° to 360° identifies the reflex sector correctly.
Vertically opposite angles are equal, so x = 124°. Both drawn lines have opposite collinear arms; the upper and lower marked sectors each measure 124°.
b + 2b + 3b + 210 = 360 gives 6b = 150 and b = 25. The unknown angles are 25°, 50° and 75°; together with 210° they total 360°. All drawn sectors match.
The split upper angle is 32° + 54° = 86°. Its vertically opposite angle is therefore x = 86°. The splitting ray and opposite collinear arms match these relationships.
